task: Write a short briefing (3 sentences) for a new engineer on why CI/CD for ML is harder than regular CI/CD.
final_answer: ML CI/CD must test three independent inputs — code, data, and hyperparameters — not just code, so a green build on code alone can still ship a broken system. Training is non-deterministic (random init, GPU order), so your tests must tolerate small variations rather than demand bit-exact outputs. And unlike ordinary bugs, a degraded model fails silently — there is no exception, only slightly worse predictions — so evaluation on slice metrics becomes mandatory. [doc4_cicd_ml.md]

hits.text: Traditional CI/CD tests code. If the unit tests pass and integration tests pass, you ship. ML systems have three independent inputs that can change behavior: code, data, and model hyperparameters...

Model behavior is non-deterministic in ways that code usually is not. The same training code run on the same data can produce slightly different models due to random initialization, GPU nondeterminism...
Models degrade silently. A traditional bug throws an exception or produces obviously wrong output. A degraded model produces subtly worse predictions...
Monitoring deployed machine learning models is essential because model quality degrades over time...
